propositions: Author a project-owned code-review criterion `project.review-phase-boundaries` that enforces phase-ownership boundaries: Pass 1 discovers only, Pass 2 verifies only, Pass 3 decides deterministically, Pass 4 coaches non-prescriptively.

The criterion must emit grounded findings for boundary violations (remediation in Pass 1, new discoveries in Pass 2, LLM discretion in Pass 3, re-adjudication in Pass 4) and abstain on legitimate refinements (narrowed discovery scope, strengthened evidence rules, atomic Pass-2 questions, deterministic Pass-3 thresholds, non-prescriptive Pass-4 coaching).

Implement single-turn routing with `exec: 1-TURN`, advisory posture (`blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.90`), and structured `code_review_findings` output containing grounded evidence without severity, confidence, or suggested_fix fields.

Build a balanced twelve-case eval corpus with six must-fire cases (RP-F1..RP-F6 covering Pass-1 assessment/policy/remediation leaks, Pass-2 ownership leaks, LLM Pass-3 discretion, and Pass-4 re-adjudication) and six must-not-fire cases (RP-N1..RP-N6 covering legitimate refinements and unchanged grandfathered debt).

Achieve perfect calibration across three live runs: recall 1.0, false_accept 0.0, agreement 1.0, minimum per-case stability ≥2/3, and Cohen kappa ≥0.70; record model, timestamp, all 36 executions, and aggregate metrics on this ticket.

Restrict implementation changes to project-owned assets (.rebar/ prompt/routing/eval, .gitignore exceptions, criterion tests, and docs/llm-framework.md subsection) with no kernel or blocking-policy changes; land on main before downstream dependencies activate.
